nodes.name: Memory is a shared home for a team’s knowledge: Markdown…
nodes.text: Memory is a shared home for a team’s knowledge: Markdown files such as `AGENTS.md`, `ENGINEERING.md` or `MARKETING.md`, plus the private assets that go with them—logos, palettes, fonts, audio and other files the team reuses. It is our first product and the most developed one, available today in invite-only early access.

nodes.name: The goal is narrow on purpose. Memory does not try to be a…
nodes.text: The goal is narrow on purpose. Memory does not try to be a wiki for everything. It keeps the decisions and instructions that people and agents need to do their work, in a form both can read and maintain.

nodes.name: Every saved change becomes an immutable revision with its…
nodes.text: Every saved change becomes an immutable revision with its author. A write names the revision it was based on; if someone else saved in the meantime, the write fails with a conflict and the writer reads the newer version first. Nobody’s work disappears because two people edited at once.

nodes.name: When a change comes from a different member than the last…
nodes.text: When a change comes from a different member than the last author, Memory can reconcile wording and duplication before the change is applied. It is careful about what it does not do: when two decisions contradict each other, it surfaces the contradiction instead of inventing a resolution. Consecutive edits by the same person skip this step entirely.

nodes.name: Access in Memory is per resource. Senior access allows…
nodes.text: Access in Memory is per resource. Senior access allows direct edits. Junior access submits proposals that a Senior reviews. The same person can be Senior on one file and Junior on another, and workspace administration is a separate responsibility from content access.

nodes.name: A proposal is not the current file. It becomes current…
nodes.text: A proposal is not the current file. It becomes current only after an authorized approval of that exact candidate against its exact base. A Senior working in the browser may approve their own proposal; an agent never approves the proposals of the member it represents. These rules apply in the same way whether the change came from a person, from Null or from an external agent.

nodes.name: Search matches names and saved contents inside a location…
nodes.text: Search matches names and saved contents inside a location and its child projects, and only returns files you can currently read. Files carry free-form tags—suggested automatically for saved files, and replaceable by hand—so a team can filter by topic or platform without inventing a fixed taxonomy.

nodes.name: Assets live beside files in the same folder tree. They are…
nodes.text: Assets live beside files in the same folder tree. They are private, checksum-verified and served only through access checks. Image previews use smaller versions made for the size they are shown at, behind the same check as the original.

nodes.name: Memory is reachable from the browser, the HTTP API, the…
nodes.text: Memory is reachable from the browser, the HTTP API, the MCP server and the CLI. Connect Codex, Claude Code or another MCP-capable harness, approve the connection in the browser, and the agent can discover locations, read files, propose changes and—if you allow it—apply them. Inside the console, Null offers Read and Work modes over the same operations.

nodes.name: For services and scripts, a private workspace API key can…
nodes.text: For services and scripts, a private workspace API key can carry read-only Memory access on behalf of the member who created it. The open source client SDKs use that to search and read Memory from your own applications.
